title: Guided Flow Policy: Learning from High-Value Actions in Offline Reinforcement Learning
claim: Two mutually guiding policies and a critic form a loop that focuses regularization on high-value data rather than all of it.
layout: Left input sidebar plus three-node cycle around a central hub; arrows show mutual influence
description: A gray sidebar on the left, titled 'Offline RL inputs at a given state s', shows two pink squares. One has contour blobs for the unknown behavior distribution. The other has red crosses for dataset actions. On the right are three large rounded blobs. The yellow one at the top is the flow policy, with a t=0 to t=1 arrow above four small density panels that evolve step by step. The green one at the bottom right is the one-step actor, with two panels linked by an arrow. The gray one at the bottom left is the critic, showing a blurry value map. A double-bordered 'Guidance g_η(s,·)' box sits in the center. Thick arrows link the parts: Distillation from flow policy to actor, an actor-critic loop, arrows from critic and actor into guidance, and guidance up to the flow policy. A dotted arrow is labeled 'Optional, see Eq. 7'. Color coding distinguishes components, and the eye goes first to the top flow-policy blob.
caption: Overview of the Guided Flow Policy framework. GFP consists of three main components: (i) in yellow, VaBC, a multi-step flow policy πω trained via weighted BC using the guidance term gη, (ii) in green, a one-step actor πθ distilled from the flow policy, and (iii) in gray, a critic Qϕ guiding action evaluation. πω regularizes the actor toward high-value actions from the dataset D; in turn, the actor shapes the flow and optimizes the critic following the actor–critic approach. The different components of the figure are introduced throughout the paper. Each drawing represents the probability distribution of actions a ∈A of a policy, in a current state s, except for the gray ones, where it is the value of actions a ∈A in state s, according to the critic.
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning often relies on behavior regularization that enforces policies to remain close to the dataset distribution. However, such approaches fail to distinguish between high-value and low-value actions in their regularization components. We introduce Guided Flow Policy (GFP), which couples a multi-step flow-matching policy with a distilled one-step actor. The actor directs the flow policy through weighted behavior cloning to focus on cloning high-value actions from the dataset rather than indiscriminately imitating all state-action pairs. In turn, the flow policy constrains the actor to remain aligned with the dataset's best transitions while maximizing the critic. This mutual guidance enables GFP to achieve state-of-the-art performance across 144 state and pixel-based tasks from the OGBench, Minari, and D4RL benchmarks, with substantial gains on suboptimal datasets and challenging tasks. Webpage: https://simple-robotics.github.io/publications/guided-flow-policy/
